games.name: Falling Orchard
games.status: conditionally accepted design by independent uniqueness and depth reviewers; implementation, ordinary-input play and remediated-baseline recheck pending
games.core: Remove an orthogonally connected same-symbol group; unsupported cells fall and empty columns close, changing which future groups exist.
games.stateActions: A visible 7×7 symbol board, remaining cells and score. Preview any group of at least two; confirm removes it, settles columns downward, then slides empty columns left. Undo restores the complete prior board. No new cells spawn.
games.decisions: Clear a cheap obstructing group to join separated larger groups, or preserve it as support so another group does not split. Removal order changes both adjacency and future legal actions.
games.depth: Three authored boards require respectively vertical joining, horizontal column closure, and a sacrifice that temporarily lowers maximum available group size. Replay optimizes remaining cells and group-square score; no board may be solved by repeatedly taking the largest group.
games.winLoss: Win by clearing the authored board. A nonempty board with no group of two is a natural dead end; offer undo or retry and label it explicitly.
games.controls: Tap/click a cell to preview its group; Confirm removes. Arrow keys navigate cells, Enter previews, native button activation confirms. Separate undo/restart buttons; no global Space handler.
games.accessibility: Each cell has a letter and texture, row/column label, selected-group membership and size. After collapse announce moved columns and remaining cells; provide a row text table. No timer or essential animation.
qa: On the horizontal-join study, complete a full keyboard win using column closure; record public actions and visible board after every removal.
On a supplied losing branch, remove the tempting large group and continue until isolated singletons remain; verify natural dead-end, no false victory, and undo recovery.
Tap-only mobile: preview one group, cancel, preview another, remove once; ensure one activation produces one removal and focus survives collapse.

existingNeighbors.difference: Flood fill recolors one permanently growing region; this removes arbitrary existing groups and gravity changes the board topology.
No directional mass slide, equal-pair fusion or spawn; irreversible selective removal and column collapse are the decisions.

proposalNeighbors: C match-three: swaps must create a line; A01 selects an existing connected group. Cross-review needed so both are not implemented as generic click-to-delete clusters.
risks: Curated complete-clear boards can be tedious if singleton traps are opaque; show preview and undo.

games.name: Corner Cabinet
games.status: conditionally accepted design by independent uniqueness and depth reviewers; implementation, ordinary-input play and remediated-baseline recheck pending
games.core: Solve a 2×2 twist cube by quarter-turning faces; each move simultaneously permutes and reorients several shared corner cubies.
games.stateActions: Eight corner identities and orientations, six labeled face views. Choose face and clockwise/counterclockwise quarter-turn. View rotation changes camera only. Undo and restart available.
games.decisions: Temporarily break an assembled face to place another corner; choose short commutator sequences that restore protected pieces while changing others. Greedily maximizing matching stickers can prevent progress.
games.depth: Three reachable scrambles isolate corner orientation, permutation and their coupling; introductory move diagrams explain notation. Later scrambles must require interleaving at least three face axes and revisiting a previously matched face. Optional move record supports replay without a harsh timer.
games.winLoss: All six faces uniform is success, independent of whole-cube orientation. Unsolved certification is a recoverable failure naming mismatched corner groups; no invented terminal loss.
games.controls: Tap a face and explicit clockwise/counterclockwise buttons. Keyboard face buttons and native activation; optional letter shortcuts only when cube surface has focus. Complete unfolded net is always usable.
games.accessibility: Letters and textures identify all six faces; describe each corner's identity, current slot and orientation in a table. No mandatory drag, 3D motion or color discrimination.
qa: Complete every public scramble with ordinary face controls and no solver/state access; include a win that breaks and restores an already uniform face.
Turn one face from solved, certify and verify failure; four identical quarter-turns restore the exact state and certificate.
Rotate camera during a partial solve and verify cube state and move count do not change; test whole-cube-equivalent solved orientations.

existingNeighbors.difference: That rotates one rigid cube by travel; stickers never permute relative to one another. Here cubies move internally and no travel board exists.
No vacancy or single-tile slide; noncommuting face turns simultaneously change corner orientation and permutation.
Pieces are coupled across faces; independent reference matching cannot solve them.

proposalNeighbors: A08 signed-prefix sorting operates on a linear stack; it lacks shared three-dimensional corner orientations. Both need independent action-level review.
risks: Can overwhelm newcomers; short teachable scrambles and full net mandatory.
Do not replace the real corner model with six independent rotate-to-match dials.

games.core: Simplify an unknot diagram through legal Reidemeister loop, bigon and strand-slide moves while preserving over/under topology.
games.stateActions: An oriented closed strand with crossing identities and signed over/under visits. Select a local region and one legal move: remove/add curl, remove/add crossing pair, or slide a strand across a crossing. Every move updates the actual embedding and crossing log.
games.decisions: A locally removable curl can expose a useful bigon, but some diagrams first require a crossing-preserving type-III slide or a temporary type-II addition. Reducing visible crossings immediately is not a universal policy.
games.depth: Authored unknots introduce the three moves, then combine nested and interleaved obstructions. At least one later diagram has no immediate reducing move and needs rearrangement. No nontrivial knot is mislabeled solvable.
games.winLoss: Win at a single crossing-free closed loop. An illegal strand-through-strand edit is refused with the exact obstruction; a failed simplification certificate remains recoverable. Optional challenge move budget only after untimed learning.
games.controls: Select numbered local regions and choose a named move; touch uses large region buttons rather than precision pulling. Keyboard visits the same regions, previews before commit, and can undo.
games.accessibility: Crossings carry IDs, explicit over/under labels and an ordered traversal list. A text explanation says which arcs and crossings each move changes. Reduced motion uses before/after diagrams.
qa: Ordinary-input win on a diagram with no initially removable curl or bigon; record a necessary type-III move and later reduction.
Attempt cancellation of two crossings with incompatible over/under order; confirm refusal leaves the state identical.
Apply a valid move and inverse, then compare traversal/crossings and keyboard focus. Full screen-reader usability requires actual review, not just SVG labels.

existingNeighbors.difference: Loose Ends swaps graph vertex locations and ignores crossing topology; this preserves knot type and manipulates over/under crossings with local topological laws.

proposalNeighbors: A05 hinge movement preserves physical linkage rather than strand crossing topology; no shared engine is assumed.
risks: Highest explanatory and geometry implementation risk in this batch; reject if legal moves are only opaque preauthored next-step buttons.
Need genuine branched local choices, verified topology and accessible arc descriptions before acceptance.

games.name: Compass House
games.status: conditionally accepted design by independent uniqueness and depth reviewers; implementation, ordinary-input play and remediated-baseline recheck pending
games.core: Construct exact geometric objects from given points using an unmarked straightedge, fixed-radius transfer and circle intersections.
games.stateActions: Given labeled points plus derived points, lines and circles with provenance. Choose Line through two points, Circle at a point through another point, or select an intersection. Arbitrary screen coordinates cannot create certified points.
games.decisions: Choose reusable auxiliary circles and intersections so later constructions share work. Distinguish a geometric locus from a merely close visual guess, and use dependency chains to construct an otherwise unavailable point.
games.depth: Progress from a perpendicular bisector to circumcenter and a tangent construction. Each later study must require multiple dependent constructions and offer more than one valid method; optional par encourages reuse, not one memorized button sequence.
games.winLoss: Win when a derived object exactly meets the geometric target predicate. Invalid/degenerate constructions and a wrong submitted object produce precise recoverable failures; no coordinate-tolerance guessing or lives.
games.controls: Select tool, then labeled objects by taps or keyboard list. Intersection candidates are separate buttons. Zoom is optional, and undo removes downstream dependents with an announced preview.
games.accessibility: All objects have names and incidence/provenance text. Circle center/radius endpoints and intersection relations are readable. Do not rely on subtle line overlap, drag precision or color.
qa: From points A and B, use equal-radius circles centered at A/B, select both intersections, draw their line, and certify the perpendicular bisector through ordinary controls.
On the circumcenter study, construct two side bisectors, select their intersection and certify; a visibly near but nonconstructed location must never be selectable as a certified point.
Submit AB as its own perpendicular bisector and verify explained failure. Try line A–A and confirm no degenerate object or consumed step.

existingNeighbors.difference: Copies cells across a known seam; this derives new geometric loci through construction dependencies.
That chooses rectangle corners on a fixed grid; this synthesizes points that do not initially exist.

proposalNeighbors: A06 divides material by irreversible cuts, with no construction of auxiliary geometry.
risks: Exact or robust symbolic geometric predicates are essential; accepting nearby clicks destroys the core.
Known geometry tasks need readable demonstrations and more than one nontrivial construction per game.

games.name: Fair Portions
games.status: conditionally accepted design by independent uniqueness and depth reviewers; implementation, ordinary-input play and remediated-baseline recheck pending
games.core: Use a limited number of straight guillotine cuts on connected pieces of an irregular, nonuniform sheet to produce specified equal-mass portions with protected emblems.
games.stateActions: A polygonal sheet with exact cellwise density and labeled protected emblems. Choose one existing piece and two boundary points from an explicit rational-coordinate lattice; preview a straight cut, then commit. Each cut replaces one piece by its two polygonal children. Cuts cannot cross an emblem.
games.decisions: An early cut establishes which later cuts are even possible. Choose whether to split a future multi-portion region or isolate a finished portion; equal area is insufficient where density differs. Cutting one portion exactly can strand the remaining mass in an unsplittable shape.
games.depth: Three studies: four equal portions from an L-sheet, unequal density with four portions, and emblem constraints requiring a non-greedy first cut. Display exact piece masses after preview; no hidden physics guessing.
games.winLoss: Win with the requested portion count, exact mass per piece and one intact emblem each. Irreversible over-cut or remaining cut budget incapable of reaching the target count ends that attempt with undo/retry available.
games.controls: Select piece and boundary point buttons, then Cut. Keyboard lists lattice points in perimeter order; touchscreen need not drag a thin line. Undo restores the parent polygon.
games.accessibility: List piece vertices, rational mass, contained emblems and cut endpoints; use patterns and numeric density labels. Preview reports the two proposed masses and forbidden emblem intersection.
qa: Complete all portions by ordinary endpoint selections, including one density study where equal-area slicing fails but equal-mass slicing succeeds.
Commit a legal first cut that strands an emblem with too much mass, then reach a natural unusable final partition; certify rejects and undo recovers.
Attempt a line tangent to a corner or passing through an emblem; verify no zero-area sliver, lost mass or accidental cut.

existingNeighbors.difference: Static axis-aligned rectangle cover from anchor counts; this progressively changes material topology through guillotine cuts of arbitrary polygon pieces and mass conservation.
Places supplied intervals; this creates portions and their feasible future cuts.

proposalNeighbors: A04 constructs auxiliary loci; A06 never adds reusable derived geometry. C cutting proposals require comparison before acceptance.
risks: Potential overlap with C cutting game and Parcel Survey if reduced to selecting independent final regions.
Need coupled non-greedy authored instances; equal rectangles alone are rejected.

games.name: Words That Move
games.status: conditionally accepted design by independent uniqueness and depth reviewers; implementation, ordinary-input play and remediated-baseline recheck pending
games.core: Push physical noun/property words into readable rules that dynamically change which objects move, block, transform and satisfy the goal.
games.stateActions: Grid contains ordinary objects and movable words. Contiguous NOUN–IS–PROPERTY lines define rules simultaneously; YOU controls every object with that property, PUSH permits pushing, STOP blocks, WIN supplies goal contact. Each directional input resolves current rules, movement and then rebuilt rules.
games.decisions: Break the current control or obstacle rule only after arranging a successor; move multiple controlled objects to transport words; turn a blocking object into a goal or a movable tool. Rule words themselves occupy and constrain space.
games.depth: Three compact studies require changing an interaction, transferring control, and managing simultaneous control. No level may be solved while leaving the initial rule set unchanged. A fourth optional puzzle supports multiple semantic solutions.
games.winLoss: Win when a YOU object touches a WIN object. No remaining YOU object or a sealed unreachable rule configuration is a recoverable dead end; always allow undo. No arbitrary move budget.
games.controls: Directional touch pad or board-focused arrows; undo and restart buttons. Tab explores the board/rule list without taking a turn. No text typing required.
games.accessibility: Every object and word has a visible text label. Live rule list announces added/removed rules and controlled-object locations. A text grid supports inspection without animation.
qa: Ordinary-input win on each study, recording the changed rule that was necessary; a rule-frozen control run must be demonstrably unwinnable by authored topology, not merely fail a random probe.
Push YOU out of every valid rule, verify explicit no-control dead end, then undo restores control and all prior rules.
Build two simultaneous YOU rules and verify one action moves both consistently; a focused Undo button activated with Space undoes exactly once and does not move the board.

existingNeighbors.difference: Sokoban has fixed player/box/goal behavior; rules here are physical manipulable objects and can change the action semantics and identity of the winning condition.
String substitutions follow an external fixed rule list; these on-board sentences are executable rules governing the spatial world that moves them.
Fixed circuit socket functions do not change the available movement actions or player identity.

proposalNeighbors: D formal-rule manipulation must be symbolic proof/semantics, not spatial executable rule pushing.
risks: Most complex state resolution in this batch; define simultaneous push conflicts, transformations and rule precedence explicitly before implementation.

games.name: Turn the Stack
games.status: conditionally accepted design by independent uniqueness and depth reviewers; implementation, ordinary-input play and remediated-baseline recheck pending
games.core: Sort distinct signed discs with a spatula that reverses and flips the entire top prefix of a stack.
games.stateActions: A linear stack of seven to ten numbered discs, each face marked up/down. Select a cut below disc k; Flip reverses the first k entries and negates their orientations. No individual swaps, lifts or arbitrary reordering.
games.decisions: Expose a desired disc, choose its orientation before sinking it into place, and avoid disturbing a completed suffix. A flip simultaneously changes order and face orientation of all affected discs.
games.depth: Teach a one-disc orientation correction, then signed permutation with repeated access to deep discs. Later named challenge certification has a proven attainable flip limit below the fixed three-flips-per-disc routine; exploiting multi-disc substructure is mandatory. Offer untimed free practice separately. Author must show at least two distinct near-optimal plans and a genuine choice that changes attainable cost.
games.winLoss: Win in increasing size with every marked face up within the named challenge flip limit. Wrong orientation/order or exceeding the limit yields a recoverable failed attempt; undo/retry available. Free practice is explicitly distinct from completing the challenge.
games.controls: Tap a boundary or choose prefix length with numeric controls, then Flip. Keyboard boundaries are buttons; preview lists resulting prefix before commit. Undo supported.
games.accessibility: Disc numbers and UP/DOWN text, not only shading. Announce selected prefix length and resulting top-to-bottom order. No dragging or speed requirement.
qa: Complete a signed-stack fixture through native controls, including a necessary one-disc flip and a multi-disc reversal; record final order and orientations.
Submit correctly ordered discs with one face down; reject without calling it solved. Flip the same prefix twice and verify exact restoration.
On mobile select a deep boundary, change selection without flipping, then commit; only one operation and move increment occurs.

Complete the final challenge through ordinary UI within its displayed bound; separately play the straightforward isolate-each-largest-disc routine and verify it exhausts the bound before success. If both pass, tighten/re-author before acceptance.

existingNeighbors.difference: That transfers one top item among capacity-limited stacks; here one action reverses and reorients an inseparable prefix and there are no destination stacks.
No blank-cell routing; operations affect a whole signed prefix.
Adjacent swaps preserve each gear orientation; prefix reversal couples many positions and signs.

proposalNeighbors: A02 also uses noncommuting permutations; reviewers must confirm signed-prefix planning feels different enough from face-turn corner restoration.
risks: Potential algorithmic repetition. Reject a game consisting only of larger stacks solved by identical three-flips-per-disc routine; short optimal-par challenges must create genuine reuse decisions.

games.name: One Last Marble
games.status: conditionally accepted design by independent uniqueness and depth reviewers; implementation, ordinary-input play and remediated-baseline recheck pending
games.core: Fling a marble along a row or column into a distant marble; impacts transfer motion along the line and eject the last marble, leaving the striker near contact.
games.stateActions: Fixed grid containing marbles with empty spaces. Choose marble and cardinal direction. A launch is legal only if another marble lies beyond at least one gap. Motion propagates through collisions; exactly the outward final marble exits, and the others settle at their contact-adjacent positions.
games.decisions: Choose which contact chain to alter so future launches retain a gap and align remaining marbles. An immediately available ejection can leave the survivors adjacent or diagonally isolated with no legal launch.
games.depth: Three authored boards require horizontal-to-vertical setup, use of a multi-impact chain, and temporarily relocating the future final survivor. Every board needs order planning, not just any available elimination.
games.winLoss: One marble remaining wins. Two or more marbles with no legal separated contact is a natural dead end; show why each potential direction fails, permit undo.
games.controls: Select marble, then one of four direction buttons; keyboard grid focus and explicit directions. Preview the whole impact chain before commit. Animation may be skipped.
games.accessibility: Number marbles and rows/columns; the preview lists each contact, final positions and ejected marble. Selection and legal direction states are explicit text.
qa: Complete a board through ordinary inputs using a multi-impact chain that sets up a perpendicular later launch.
Follow the authored tempting first ejection into a no-launch terminal state; verify no victory with two marbles and undo restores a playable state.
Try launching into an adjacent marble and off the board without a target; both must leave all positions unchanged.

existingNeighbors.difference: Peg solitaire moves the jumper to a fixed empty destination and removes the jumped midpoint; impacts here transfer motion across variable gaps, relocate several pieces and eject the final contact.
A lone slider stops against walls while collecting targets; collision transfer changes the population and geometry of all future actions.

proposalNeighbors: C billiards/pool should retain continuous aim/friction; this is a discrete contact-transfer puzzle without aim strength.
risks: Must not simplify into jump-over-an-adjacent-piece elimination, which would duplicate Peg.
Exact collision endpoint rules need diagrams and source-independent UI examples before coding.

Reverse insertion on the immediately previous lane is forbidden.
games.decisions: Shift a target closer while preserving an escape route, carry the player with a displaced tile, and choose where to finish before the next insertion. The spare's outgoing shape constrains the next topology change.
games.depth: Three studies require carrying a target, deliberate player displacement and cycling a useful corner tile through the spare. Authored insertion budgets allow multiple plans but rule out simply shifting one lane repeatedly.
games.winLoss: Collect the ordered objectives and return home before the insertion budget is exhausted. Illegal insertion or disconnected walk is refused. Budget exhaustion is an explained loss with replay.
games.controls: Rotate/insert buttons around board; movement by destination selection from reachable cells or arrow-by-arrow path. Keyboard list includes insertion ports. Walking and insertion phases clearly separated.
games.accessibility: Each tile exposes corridor ports and coordinate, spare tile labeled, selected insertion announces which line and occupants will move. Text reachability list available.

Try reversing the previous insertion and walking across an unconnected seam; reject without shifting tiles or advancing phase.

Routes in an existing fixed graph; here the action rebuilds the graph and relocates its contents.

games.core: Move atoms that automatically form persistent bonds on contact, turning separate movable objects into rigid molecules whose expanding footprint must navigate the room.

Bonds cannot be cut; undo can reverse a move. Goal specifies molecular connectivity and delivery region.
games.decisions: Choose assembly order and approach side so an early bond does not consume a valence needed later or create a shape too wide for an exit. A loose atom can pass a corridor before it becomes part of a larger rigid body.
games.depth: Three studies require delayed assembly, branch attachment from a particular side and transporting components separately before final bonding. At least one wrong legal bond creates a provable valence dead end.
games.winLoss: Win with the required connectivity and all product atoms in the dock. Wrong saturated connectivity or an undeliverable rigid product is a recoverable dead end; certify explains missing/extra bonds.
games.controls: Select atom/molecule, use cardinal controls. Keyboard can select atoms from a list and move with focused direction controls. Preview candidate bonds and combined footprint before commit.
games.accessibility: Atoms carry symbol, ID and capacity/used-valence text. Provide a bond adjacency list and footprint coordinates, with explicit selection of the whole connected molecule.
qa: Win the narrow-exit study by moving separate components through before assembling them; no hidden-state solver or debug placement.
Make the available but wrong saturating bond, certify failure with exact obstructed target bond, undo and finish legitimately.
Select a bonded atom, move once and verify all atoms in that component translate equally; a collision by any member rejects the whole move.

existingNeighbors.difference: Crates never join and player pushes individual objects; this directly moves whole connected components whose shape and future legal moves change irreversibly when they bond.

risks: Bond order cannot be ambiguous when several contacts form at once; deterministic rules and previews required.
Reject if moving single atoms to obvious final sockets suffices without planning an intermediate molecular footprint.

Capture before moving a box, then move it and paste; the pasted patch must reflect capture-time state, not the current source. Attempt avatar overwrite and verify atomic refusal.

games.name: Gathering Grounds
games.core: Finite-horizon bandit exploration versus productive exploitation
games.stateActions: Each day harvest one of three teaching beds or four later-study beds, initially unknown. Harvest earns actual baskets and reveals that bed’s current yield; displayed history persists. Beds have public process classes (stable, depleting, recovering), but which class belongs where is initially unknown. A costly soil survey reveals process class without yielding baskets.
games.decisions: Spend scarce days learning a potentially superior bed or keep collecting known yield; revisit recovering beds after rest, and stop exploiting a depleting bed before it is exhausted.
games.depth: No final identification question. Good information is useful only through harvest decisions that follow. Changing horizon and depleted/recovered conditions make both early surveying and immediate harvest rational in different authored scenarios.
games.winLoss: Earn basket quota by the fixed final day; falling short loses naturally. Quotas are calibrated so ordinary informed choices can succeed across every allowed hidden assignment, not only lucky seeds.

games.name: Loop Transit
games.core: Passenger service topology design with autonomous transfers and finite fleet
games.stateActions: Draw up to three cyclic lines by selecting station sequences. Allocate trains and carriage capacities; advance one public demand pulse to move trains, board waiting passengers, and route transfers. Editing an occupied line requires spending a relocation token or waiting until its train empties.
games.decisions: Choose direct versus interchange service, size bottleneck capacity, and avoid long loops that strand a low-volume branch. A connectivity solution alone can fail due to wait and train phase.
games.depth: Stations add destinations and demand changes publicly. Different feasible line topologies trade transfer congestion against coverage and journey time; score passenger completion and worst queue.
games.winLoss: Serve the target number through twelve pulses while no station exceeds its platform capacity; a platform spillover fails. All demand pulses are shown ahead and remain turn based.
